name: BSP_MainMenuScreen_Construct
evidence: Hypothesis, not a recovered symbol. __fastcall(this) returning this, SEH frame, RET. The 578h screen at 00E198AC+58h, built first by 00686380. Chains BSP_FrontEndScreen_Construct (004F7180), then installs primary vtable 00CEFC5C at +00h and secondary vtables 00CEFC48 at +08h, 00CEFC24 at +0Ch and 00CEFC04 at +40h, zeroes the field runs from +74h to +510h, builds a five-element eh_vector array at +134h, and closes by clearing 00E194C4..00E194D0 and setting 00E08874 (the main-menu page) to 1. Slot +00h of 00CEFC5C is 00590570, a 'mov eax,1; ret' leaf, so the screen id is 1 = INTF_MAINMENU in the 00E08CD8 table. Virtuals: +0Ch 00590D60, +10h 00582F30 (register, chains 004F71D0), +14h 005861B0 (binds FE_main and FE_main_listbox), +18h 005987F0, +1Ch 0058F560, +20h 00599DB0, +24h 005905E0. The existing 'cg_array_ctor_helper' tag on this address is wrong: this is a class constructor, not a compiler array-construction helper. See docs/MAIN_MENU_SCREENS.md.

name: BSP_MainMenuScreen_FillActiveList
evidence: Hypothesis, not a recovered symbol. Vtable +24h of the main-menu screen at 00E198AC+58h. Five instructions read from the listing: ADD ECX,470h; PUSH ECX; MOV ECX,[ESP+8]; CALL 004D6790; RET 4. So it is __thiscall(this, void* sink) and calls 004D6790 with ECX = the stack argument and this+470h as the argument; Ghidra's decompilation drops the ECX swap. 004D6790 is the same routine BSP_Frontend_UpdateActiveScreens calls and is tagged stl_probable, and the +470h sub-object is the one the register virtual 00582F30 hides through its virtual +34h. docs/MAIN_MENU_SCREEN_UPDATE.md.

name: BSP_MainMenu_PlaySelectedMission

Flushes the award tracker (004E1CA0 then 00690CD0), takes the record from 005806A0, and branches on the size dword of the MovieName string at record+58h (00592325): with a movie it runs 005830A0, 00A85C00(ECX = [00E198AC]+50h), the manager virtual +0Ch, sets the two bytes at [00E18D48]+4h/+5h, 004F83B0, the movie virtual +18h, 004F8A20(&record+58h, 1, [00CEFCB8], 0) at 00592383, [00E18D48]+30h = 1, and hands 0058D9D0 to 004F8970 at 0059239C; without one it calls 0058BDF0 at 005923B3 and clears the help line through 0054B530 at 0059244C. Five callers. See docs/MISSION_BRIEFING_START.md. | Run-time evidence, bsp_game.exe milestone 2e (packet cc_exe_2e). Ran as the mission-detail page's play action for USN02. The record's MovieName is empty on this installation, so 00592325 took the no-movie arm and called 0058BDF0 directly, which is the arm the reconstruction reports as false.

name: BSP_MainMenuScreen_BuildMissionListPage
evidence: Hypothesis, not a recovered symbol. __thiscall void(MainMenuScreen* this, int page), RET 4, SEH frame, 1081 instructions. Writes the requested page to 00E08874 at 005978A7 and is the only site that produces pages 4..8. Five arms, each assigning a title, publishing a group index to 00E194D8 and copying one mission-group widget handle into +110h: page 4 FE.ijn_campaign (005978FE) / group 1 (00597957) / +314h missions_JP_Group (00597961); page 5 FE.usn_campaign (00597987) / group 2 (005979E0) / +310h (005979EA); page 6 FE.main_ijn_dlc_title (00597A75) / group 3 (00597AD3) / +31Ch (00597AD9); page 7 FE.main_usn_dlc_title (00597AFC) / group 4 (00597B3C) / +318h (00597B42); page 8 FE.training_grounds (00597A05) / group 0 (00597A55) / +320h training_Group (00597A5B). The campaign bytes are +564h (United States) and +565h (downloadable content). This settles the MainMenuPage naming: 4 is Japan and 5 is the United States, not the reverse. See docs/MAIN_MENU_MISSION_DETAIL.md.

name: BSP_MainMenu_HandleBack
evidence: Hypothesis, not a recovered symbol. __fastcall(this), ECX = the main-menu screen 005902E0. Dispatches on the main-menu page at 00E08874. Page 1 calls 00588A80, which carries FE_pc.main_quit_confirm, so the top-level back is the quit confirmation. Pages 4, 5, 6 and 7 form one group tested in that order at 00598B7B..00598B9C: it caches 00A9C990's result into 00E08878 and 00E194DC and writes 1 into screen+55Ch for 5 and 7 only, which is what marks those two as the downloadable-content arms of the campaign mission list. The remaining arms reach BSP_MenuCommandScreen_GetSingleton with composed strings. Read to the dispatch only; the arms past 00598FA0 were not followed. See docs/MAIN_MENU_SCREENS.md. | CORRECTION (packet cc_menu_detail): the routine runs on this = screen + 8, not on the screen. 00598BD4 reaches the top-level list box as [EDI+1B0h] (screen+1B8h) and 00598FBF recovers the screen with LEA ESI,[EDI-8]. Every offset in the decompilation is therefore 8 low. The byte stored at 00598FB3 as +55Ch is screen+564h, the United States campaign flag that 00597870 and 0058C010 also set on pages 5 and 7; it is not a downloadable-content flag. The downloadable-content flag is screen+565h (00597AEE, 00597B4A). The campaign arm ends at 00599315/00599318 by clearing screen+5Ch and calling 0058C010, so this is also how the mission-detail page is entered. See docs/MAIN_MENU_MISSION_DETAIL.md.

name: BSP_MainMenuScreen_Update
evidence: Hypothesis, not a recovered symbol. Update virtual of the main-menu screen at 00e198ac+58h (class constructed by 005902e0, screen id 1 INTF_MAINMENU), 2355 bytes with sixteen returns; docs/MAIN_MENU_SCREENS.md lists it as exported only. Defined from disk-verified bytes by the integrator; body not yet analyzed. | Read to the instruction at 00599DB0..0059A6E2 (docs/MAIN_MENU_SCREEN_UPDATE.md). __thiscall(this, float seconds), RET 4; the stack argument is the frame delta (FLD [ESP+0B0h] at 0059A3BD, [ESP+0B4h] at 0059A66B, both the first argument of 00588C70). Five stages: drain the +0Ch text queue when byte +10h is set; the damaged-content sweep over 00F8A304 raising FE_xbox.xsm_dlcdamaged; the downloaded-content notice gated on 00F8ABE8+30h and sign-in state 2 raising FE_xbox.xsm_dlcdownloaded; the async-text arm on page 0Ah; then the page machine on 00E08874. Actions through 004D92B0: 4Ah accept, 4Bh back, 50h context, established by matching the GUI handler 005993A0's control codes A2h/A3h/A7h arm for arm. One RET 4 at 0059A6E0; the decompiler's early returns in the page-0Ah block are string-destructor artifacts.
